name: Wattled Ibis
rangeDescription: Highlands of ethiopia
description: A dark ibis with a shaggy crest and a small wattle below the bill that is difficult to see. White patches in the wings are distinctive, especially in flight.

name: Black-breasted Hillstar
rangeDescription: Andes of peru (junín, huancavelica, ancash, lima, and ayacucho)
description: Large hummingbird found only at very high elevations in the Andes of central Peru. Male is dusky green with a sparkling green throat, a blue breast and belly, and gray sides.

name: Philippine Hawk-Cuckoo
rangeDescription: Philippines
description: A fairly large bird of lowland and montane forest. Dark gray-brown above with a rather long barred tail, a rufous chest, a gray hood, and a white throat.

name: Glow-throated Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Mountains of western panama (chiriquí and veraguas)
description: Tiny, poorly-known hummingbird with extremely limited range in western Panama. Males are greenish above with rusty flanks, a pinkish-red throat, and a white collar.

name: Rufous-vented Paradise-Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Southeastern nigeria and southern cameroon to gabon to northern angola
description: This relatively short-tailed paradise-flycatcher is often found near forest edges and around villages and towns in gardens. Both sexes have gray heads and undersides with blue bills and blue eye-rings, as well as a red back, red wings, red tail, and most importantly, a red vent.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Guianan Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Eastern venezuela, the guianas, and northeastern brazil north of the amazon river and east of the rio branco and rio negro; populations south of the amazon river (west to the lower rio madeira, eastward to ceará and alagoas) included here, but may represent an undescribed taxon
description: Tiny, inconspicuous flycatcher; in addition to small size, note stubby bill, wing bars, and longish tail. Found in a variety of forest habitats including primary and secondary rainforest, low-stature forests with sandy soils, and along river edges.

name: Chestnut-crowned Babbler
rangeDescription: Arid woodland of east-central australia
description: Large, conspicuous songbird with long decurved bill, gray mask, whitish eyebrow, chestnut crown, pale wingbars, and dark eye. White throat and breast with black border extends to upper belly; lower belly and undertail dark.

name: Biak Leaf Warbler
rangeDescription: Biak (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea)
description: A small dull-colored warbler with a greenish upperside, instinct wingbars, a pale throat, and yellowish underparts. Singles, pairs, and small groups inhabit lowland and hill forest, including secondary forest.

name: Cape Parrot
rangeDescription: Southern and eastern south africa (eastern cape and southern kwazulu-natal; isolated population at woodbush forest, limpopo)
description: Large, dark green parrot. Note the red patches on the shoulder and thighs.

name: Yemen Serin
rangeDescription: High altitude bushy hills of southwestern saudi arabia
description: Small, slim seedeater of the southern Arabian highlands. Brown overall, with a buffy face and whitish underparts.

name: Sichuan Partridge
rangeDescription: Southwestern china (hills of south-central sichuan)
description: A rare and retiring partridge of mixed forest, found only in the south-central portion of China’s Sichuan province. If seen well, combination of orange cheek patch, striped white throat, and broad maroon chest band is diagnostic.

name: Yellowish Imperial-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Bismarck archipelago including admiralty islands
description: Large pigeon, mostly yellowish-white with black wing feathers. Tip of the tail also black.

name: Syrian Serin
rangeDescription: Mountains of lebanon and syria; winters to türkiye and northwestern iraq
description: A small and elegant finch. More elongated than European Serin and much plainer.

name: Blue-chested Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Northeastern nicaragua to colombia and ecuador (west of the andes)
description: Male has glittering purple-blue throat, green back and crown, paler grayish belly, and dark tail. Female less obvious, with spotted chest; note the pink base to the lower mandible of the bill.

name: Forty-spotted Pardalote
rangeDescription: Drier sclerophyll forest of eastern tasmania and flinders island
description: Tiny greenish bird restricted to a small range in Tasmania. Primarily greenish-gray.

name: Scintillant Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Humid montane forest of costa rica and western panama
description: Small hummingbird, unique orange throat distinguishes male from all other hummingbirds in limited range. Female less obvious; she has speckled throat, orangey flanks, and all-rufous tail with black band and buffy tips.

name: Royal Penguin
rangeDescription: Macquarie island and adjacent islets
description: The largest crested penguin, with a diagnostic whitish face. Only breeds on the Australian-administered Macquarie Island; occasionally seen off of New Zealand’s subantarctic islands, rarely off of the mainland.

name: Gould's Frogmouth
rangeDescription: Peninsular thailand to malay peninsula, sumatra, borneo, and adjacent islands
description: Cryptic, seldom-seen nightbird of lowland and foothill forests. Unlike other small frogmouths, sexes are alike.

name: Javan Trogon
rangeDescription: Montane forest of western java
description: Beautiful and highly range-restricted trogon found only in Java’s far western belt of volcanoes, where it inhabits montane and foothill forests at 900-2500 meters. Unmistakable, decked out in all the colors of the rainbow: note bright red bill, yellow breast, orange belly, olive-green head and chest, glossy blue-green back, and purple-and-green bare facial skin.

name: New Zealand Falcon
rangeDescription: Locally in new zealand, including stewart and auckland islands
description: A compact raptor endemic to New Zealand, with streaky cream-and-brown breast and reddish-brown undertail. In flight, note rapid beating of long pointed wings, and long rounded tail shape while gliding.
